cards.back: The number of linearly independent rows or columns in a matrix.
A measure of how strongly solution error may amplify input or measurement error.
All linear combinations of a set of vectors.
A linearly independent set that spans the vector space.
A scalar λ for which Av=λv for some nonzero vector v.
Small perturbations decay back toward an equilibrium as time increases.
Parameter estimation that minimizes the sum of squared residuals.
Observed value minus model-predicted value.
Minimize ‖b − Ax‖²; solution satisfies the normal equations AᵀAx = Aᵀb.
Aᵀr = 0: residuals are orthogonal to the columns of A; with an intercept they sum to zero.
R² = 1 − SSR/SST; check residual patterns for curvature, saturation or outliers.
Read unknowns only inside the standards' range; uncertainty grows away from the mean.
pₙ₊₁ = M pₙ; with column vectors each column of M sums to one.
Mπ = π (eigenvalue 1); for two states π_A = (B→A)/(A→B + B→A).
Deviation shrinks by λ₂ per step; for two states λ₂ = 1 − (A→B) − (B→A).
Switching depends only on the current state; history effects need extra states.
Rank = number of independent columns = dimension of the column space; null space = {x : Ax = 0}; rank + nullity = number of columns.
Ax = b is solvable only if b is in the column space; if a solution x₀ exists, all solutions are x₀ + null space, so unknowns with a null component are not identifiable.
The solution of smallest length is orthogonal to the null space; it is a convention, not a measurement.
An intercept plus a full set of indicators is rank deficient; drop one column or impose a constraint; near-dependence is the practical version.
p = (a·b/a·a) a; the residual r = b − p is perpendicular to a; ‖b‖² = ‖p‖² + ‖r‖².
q₁ = a₁/‖a₁‖; v₂ = a₂ − (q₁·a₂)q₁; q₂ = v₂/‖v₂‖; a zero v₂ means a₂ was dependent.
A = QR with R upper triangular; solve Rx = Qᵀb by back-substitution; the residual norm is √(‖b‖² − ‖Qᵀb‖²).
AᵀA squares the condition number; QR does not form it, so it is the stable way to solve least-squares problems.
A real symmetric matrix has real eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors: A = QΛQᵀ, with trace = sum and determinant = product of the eigenvalues.
For [[a, b], [b, d]], θ = ½ atan2(2b, a − d) gives a dominant axis, modulo 180°, when the eigenvalues differ. A repeated eigenvalue has no unique dominant axis.
xᵀAx = a₁₁x₁² + 2a₁₂x₁x₂ + a₂₂x₂²; over unit vectors it ranges from λ_min to λ_max; positive definite means all eigenvalues are positive.
For a covariance matrix C and a unit vector w the variance is wᵀCw; the maximum is λ_max along its eigenvector; the total variance is the trace.

For an m × n matrix, A = UΣVᵀ with orthogonal U (m × m), V (n × n) and rectangular diagonal Σ (m × n). Positive σ² are the nonzero eigenvalues shared by AᵀA and AAᵀ; rank counts nonzero σ. Orthogonal factors can include reflections.
Eckart–Young: keep the k largest terms; the error in the Frobenius norm is √(sum of the dropped σ²); ‖A‖²_F = Σ σ².
A rank-k approximation of an m × n matrix needs k(m + n + 1) numbers instead of mn; saves storage only if k(m + n + 1) < mn; usefulness also requires acceptable error.
A very small last singular value means near rank deficiency; For full column rank, σ₁/σ_min is the 2-norm condition number; rank deficiency makes inversion nonunique.
For invertible A, κ₂ = σ_max/σ_min; fixed-A relative signal errors have a worst-case multiplier κ₂.
Small residual means a close fit to supplied data; poorly conditioned columns can still give large parameter errors.
In a singular direction ridge multiplies the unregularized coefficient by σ²/(σ² + α). This introduces bias.
Condition numbers and penalties depend on coordinate scales. Report units, scaling, calibration uncertainty and tuning.
For n sample rows, subtract column means and use C = ZᵀZ/(n − 1). Uncentered SVD answers a different question.
Score t = z·q; rank-one centered reconstruction is tq. Add the training mean to recover original coordinates.
Covariance PCA preserves the stated units; standardized PCA uses a correlation matrix and weights each variable to unit variance.
Explained variance is descriptive. Assess confounding and fit preprocessing on training data only.
For independent signal noise s²I, singular-direction parameter variance is s²/σ_i².
Averaging n independent signal pairs divides covariance by n. Shared calibration offsets do not average away.
Compare geometry using calibrated gains and a stated noise covariance; exercise the weak direction.
State units, matrix, noise assumptions, singular values, parameter uncertainty, estimator convention and independent validation.
Compute √[mean of squared Euclidean errors], using an independent reference; mean error can cancel while RMSE is large.
The lab pairs opposite errors deliberately. Its independent-noise uncertainty calculation uses a separate stated model.
An invertible two-equation model fits two noisy signals exactly; the residual does not certify displacement accuracy.
Compare weak gains, calibrated units and error covariance. Validate new reference displacements in the weak direction.
